#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u

# traceroute_internal_hosts.sh
# Run traceroute against a set of internal hostnames.
#
# Usage:
#   ./traceroute_internal_hosts.sh                 # uses HOSTS below
#   ./traceroute_internal_hosts.sh host1 host2     # uses CLI args instead
#   HOSTS_FILE=hosts.txt ./traceroute_internal_hosts.sh
#
# Edit this list for your environment.
HOSTS=(
  "gateway.internal"
  "dns.internal"
  "fileserver.internal"
  "printer.internal"
)

TRACEROUTE_BIN="${TRACEROUTE_BIN:-traceroute}"
MAX_HOPS="${MAX_HOPS:-30}"
WAIT_SECONDS="${WAIT_SECONDS:-3}"
QUERIES_PER_HOP="${QUERIES_PER_HOP:-3}"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $0 [hostname ...]

Runs traceroute for each hostname supplied. If no hostnames are supplied,
it uses HOSTS defined in the script, or HOSTS_FILE if set.

Environment variables:
  HOSTS_FILE          File containing hostnames, one per line; # comments allowed
  TRACEROUTE_BIN      traceroute binary/path (default: traceroute)
  MAX_HOPS            Max hops (default: 30)
  WAIT_SECONDS        Per-probe wait timeout in seconds (default: 3)
  QUERIES_PER_HOP     Probes per hop (default: 3)
EOF
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  usage
  exit 0
fi

if ! command -v "$TRACEROUTE_BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Error: '$TRACEROUTE_BIN' not found. Install traceroute or set TRACEROUTE_BIN=/path/to/traceroute." >&2
  exit 127
fi

if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
  HOSTS=("$@")
elif [[ -n "${HOSTS_FILE:-}" ]]; then
  if [[ ! -r "$HOSTS_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: HOSTS_FILE '$HOSTS_FILE' is not readable." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  mapfile -t HOSTS < <(grep -Ev '^\s*($|#)' "$HOSTS_FILE")
fi

if [[ ${#HOSTS[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "Error: no hosts specified." >&2
  usage >&2
  exit 1
fi

started_at="$(date -Is)"
echo "Traceroute run started: $started_at"
echo "Hosts: ${HOSTS[*]}"
echo

for host in "${HOSTS[@]}"; do
  echo "================================================================"
  echo "Traceroute to: $host"
  echo "Started: $(date -Is)"
  echo "----------------------------------------------------------------"

  if "$TRACEROUTE_BIN" -m "$MAX_HOPS" -w "$WAIT_SECONDS" -q "$QUERIES_PER_HOP" "$host"; then
    status="OK"
  else
    status="FAILED"
  fi

  echo "----------------------------------------------------------------"
  echo "Finished: $(date -Is) [$status]"
  echo
 done

echo "Traceroute run finished: $(date -Is)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail

# traceroute_internal_hosts.sh
# Run traceroute against a set of internal hostnames and capture the IP
# addresses seen at every hop in the network path.
#
# Usage:
#   ./traceroute_internal_hosts.sh                 # uses HOSTS below
#   ./traceroute_internal_hosts.sh host1 host2     # uses CLI args instead
#   HOSTS_FILE=hosts.txt ./traceroute_internal_hosts.sh
#
# Output:
#   - Full traceroute output:  $OUTPUT_DIR/<host>.traceroute.txt
#   - Hop IP CSV:             $OUTPUT_DIR/<host>.hop_ips.csv
#   - Combined hop IP CSV:    $OUTPUT_DIR/all_hop_ips.csv
#
# Edit this list for your environment.
HOSTS=(
  "gateway.internal"
  "dns.internal"
  "fileserver.internal"
  "printer.internal"
)

TRACEROUTE_BIN="${TRACEROUTE_BIN:-traceroute}"
MAX_HOPS="${MAX_HOPS:-30}"
WAIT_SECONDS="${WAIT_SECONDS:-3}"
QUERIES_PER_HOP="${QUERIES_PER_HOP:-3}"
OUTPUT_DIR="${OUTPUT_DIR:-traceroute-results-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)}"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $0 [hostname ...]

Runs traceroute for each hostname supplied. If no hostnames are supplied,
it uses HOSTS defined in the script, or HOSTS_FILE if set.

Environment variables:
  HOSTS_FILE          File containing hostnames, one per line; # comments allowed
  TRACEROUTE_BIN      traceroute binary/path (default: traceroute)
  MAX_HOPS            Max hops (default: 30)
  WAIT_SECONDS        Per-probe wait timeout in seconds (default: 3)
  QUERIES_PER_HOP     Probes per hop (default: 3)
  OUTPUT_DIR          Directory for traceroute captures and CSVs

CSV columns:
  host,hop,ip
EOF
}

sanitize_filename() {
  # Keep filenames boring and portable.
  printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_'
}

extract_hop_ips_csv() {
  local host="$1"
  local traceroute_file="$2"
  local csv_file="$3"

  printf 'host,hop,ip\n' > "$csv_file"

  # Only parse actual hop lines, which begin with a hop number. This avoids
  # treating the destination IP in traceroute's header line as a hop.
  # Captures IPv4 and common IPv6 forms. Duplicate probe replies from the same
  # hop are collapsed while preserving hop/IP pairs.
  awk -v host="$host" '
    /^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]/ {
      hop = $1
      line = $0

      # IPv4 addresses.
      while (match(line, /([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}/)) {
        ip = substr(line, RSTART, RLENGTH)
        key = hop SUBSEP ip
        if (!seen[key]++) {
          print host "," hop "," ip
        }
        line = substr(line, RSTART + RLENGTH)
      }

      # IPv6 addresses. This intentionally excludes tokens without a colon.
      # It strips common punctuation produced by traceroute formatting.
      n = split($0, fields, /[[:space:]]+/)
      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        token = fields[i]
        gsub(/[(),]/, "", token)
        if (token ~ /:/ && token ~ /^[0-9A-Fa-f:.]+$/) {
          key = hop SUBSEP token
          if (!seen[key]++) {
            print host "," hop "," token
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ' "$traceroute_file" >> "$csv_file"
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  usage
  exit 0
fi

if ! command -v "$TRACEROUTE_BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Error: '$TRACEROUTE_BIN' not found. Install traceroute or set TRACEROUTE_BIN=/path/to/traceroute." >&2
  exit 127
fi

if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
  HOSTS=("$@")
elif [[ -n "${HOSTS_FILE:-}" ]]; then
  if [[ ! -r "$HOSTS_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: HOSTS_FILE '$HOSTS_FILE' is not readable." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  mapfile -t HOSTS < <(grep -Ev '^\s*($|#)' "$HOSTS_FILE")
fi

if [[ ${#HOSTS[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "Error: no hosts specified." >&2
  usage >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"
combined_csv="$OUTPUT_DIR/all_hop_ips.csv"
printf 'host,hop,ip\n' > "$combined_csv"

started_at="$(date -Is)"
echo "Traceroute run started: $started_at"
echo "Hosts: ${HOSTS[*]}"
echo "Output directory: $OUTPUT_DIR"
echo

for host in "${HOSTS[@]}"; do
  safe_host="$(sanitize_filename "$host")"
  traceroute_file="$OUTPUT_DIR/${safe_host}.traceroute.txt"
  hop_csv="$OUTPUT_DIR/${safe_host}.hop_ips.csv"

  echo "================================================================"
  echo "Traceroute to: $host"
  echo "Started: $(date -Is)"
  echo "Raw output: $traceroute_file"
  echo "Hop IP CSV: $hop_csv"
  echo "----------------------------------------------------------------"

  if "$TRACEROUTE_BIN" -m "$MAX_HOPS" -w "$WAIT_SECONDS" -q "$QUERIES_PER_HOP" "$host" 2>&1 | tee "$traceroute_file"; then
    status="OK"
  else
    status="FAILED"
  fi

  extract_hop_ips_csv "$host" "$traceroute_file" "$hop_csv"
  tail -n +2 "$hop_csv" >> "$combined_csv"

  echo "----------------------------------------------------------------"
  echo "Captured hop IPs:"
  if [[ $(wc -l < "$hop_csv") -gt 1 ]]; then
    column -s, -t "$hop_csv" 2>/dev/null || cat "$hop_csv"
  else
    echo "No hop IPs captured. Hops may have timed out or name resolution/traceroute may have failed."
  fi
  echo "Finished: $(date -Is) [$status]"
  echo
done

echo "Combined hop IP CSV: $combined_csv"
echo "Traceroute run finished: $(date -Is)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -uo pipefail

# traceroute_internal_hosts.sh
# Run traceroute against a set of internal hostnames and capture the IP
# addresses seen at every hop in the network path.
#
# Usage:
#   ./traceroute_internal_hosts.sh                 # uses HOSTS below
#   ./traceroute_internal_hosts.sh host1 host2     # uses CLI args instead
#   HOSTS_FILE=hosts.txt ./traceroute_internal_hosts.sh
#
# Output:
#   - Full traceroute output:  $OUTPUT_DIR/<host>.traceroute.txt
#   - Hop IP CSV:             $OUTPUT_DIR/<host>.hop_ips.csv
#   - Combined hop IP CSV:    $OUTPUT_DIR/all_hop_ips.csv
#
# Edit this list for your environment.
HOSTS=(
  "gateway.internal"
  "dns.internal"
  "fileserver.internal"
  "printer.internal"
)

TRACEROUTE_BIN="${TRACEROUTE_BIN:-traceroute}"
MAX_HOPS="${MAX_HOPS:-30}"
WAIT_SECONDS="${WAIT_SECONDS:-3}"
QUERIES_PER_HOP="${QUERIES_PER_HOP:-3}"
OUTPUT_DIR="${OUTPUT_DIR:-traceroute-results-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)}"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
Usage: $0 [hostname ...]

Runs traceroute for each hostname supplied. If no hostnames are supplied,
it uses HOSTS defined in the script, or HOSTS_FILE if set.

Environment variables:
  HOSTS_FILE          File containing hostnames, one per line; # comments allowed
  TRACEROUTE_BIN      traceroute binary/path (default: traceroute)
  MAX_HOPS            Max hops (default: 30)
  WAIT_SECONDS        Per-probe wait timeout in seconds (default: 3)
  QUERIES_PER_HOP     Probes per hop (default: 3)
  OUTPUT_DIR          Directory for traceroute captures and CSVs

CSV columns:
  host,hop,ip
EOF
}

sanitize_filename() {
  # Keep filenames boring and portable.
  printf '%s' "$1" | tr -c 'A-Za-z0-9._-' '_'
}

extract_hop_ips_csv() {
  local host="$1"
  local traceroute_file="$2"
  local csv_file="$3"

  printf 'host,hop,ip\n' > "$csv_file"

  # Only parse actual hop lines, which begin with a hop number. This avoids
  # treating the destination IP in traceroute's header line as a hop.
  # Captures IPv4 and common IPv6 forms. Duplicate probe replies from the same
  # hop are collapsed while preserving hop/IP pairs.
  awk -v host="$host" '
    /^[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]/ {
      hop = $1
      line = $0

      # IPv4 addresses.
      while (match(line, /([0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}/)) {
        ip = substr(line, RSTART, RLENGTH)
        key = hop SUBSEP ip
        if (!seen[key]++) {
          print host "," hop "," ip
        }
        line = substr(line, RSTART + RLENGTH)
      }

      # IPv6 addresses. This intentionally excludes tokens without a colon.
      # It strips common punctuation produced by traceroute formatting.
      n = split($0, fields, /[[:space:]]+/)
      for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
        token = fields[i]
        gsub(/[(),]/, "", token)
        if (token ~ /:/ && token ~ /^[0-9A-Fa-f:.]+$/) {
          key = hop SUBSEP token
          if (!seen[key]++) {
            print host "," hop "," token
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ' "$traceroute_file" >> "$csv_file"
}

if [[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]]; then
  usage
  exit 0
fi

if ! command -v "$TRACEROUTE_BIN" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "Error: '$TRACEROUTE_BIN' not found. Install traceroute or set TRACEROUTE_BIN=/path/to/traceroute." >&2
  exit 127
fi

if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
  HOSTS=("$@")
elif [[ -n "${HOSTS_FILE:-}" ]]; then
  if [[ ! -r "$HOSTS_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "Error: HOSTS_FILE '$HOSTS_FILE' is not readable." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  mapfile -t HOSTS < <(grep -Ev '^\s*($|#)' "$HOSTS_FILE")
fi

if [[ ${#HOSTS[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  echo "Error: no hosts specified." >&2
  usage >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"
combined_csv="$OUTPUT_DIR/all_hop_ips.csv"
printf 'host,hop,ip\n' > "$combined_csv"

started_at="$(date -Is)"
echo "Traceroute run started: $started_at"
echo "Hosts: ${HOSTS[*]}"
echo "Output directory: $OUTPUT_DIR"
echo

for host in "${HOSTS[@]}"; do
  safe_host="$(sanitize_filename "$host")"
  traceroute_file="$OUTPUT_DIR/${safe_host}.traceroute.txt"
  hop_csv="$OUTPUT_DIR/${safe_host}.hop_ips.csv"

  echo "================================================================"
  echo "Traceroute to: $host"
  echo "Started: $(date -Is)"
  echo "Raw output: $traceroute_file"
  echo "Hop IP CSV: $hop_csv"
  echo "----------------------------------------------------------------"

  if "$TRACEROUTE_BIN" -m "$MAX_HOPS" -w "$WAIT_SECONDS" -q "$QUERIES_PER_HOP" "$host" 2>&1 | tee "$traceroute_file"; then
    status="OK"
  else
    status="FAILED"
  fi

  extract_hop_ips_csv "$host" "$traceroute_file" "$hop_csv"
  tail -n +2 "$hop_csv" >> "$combined_csv"

  echo "----------------------------------------------------------------"
  echo "Captured hop IPs:"
  if [[ $(wc -l < "$hop_csv") -gt 1 ]]; then
    column -s, -t "$hop_csv" 2>/dev/null || cat "$hop_csv"
  else
    echo "No hop IPs captured. Hops may have timed out or name resolution/traceroute may have failed."
  fi
  echo "Finished: $(date -Is) [$status]"
  echo
done

echo "Combined hop IP CSV: $combined_csv"
echo "Traceroute run finished: $(date -Is)"

  host,hop,ip

  Written to OUTPUT_DIR/network_topology_map.txt

          }
        }
      }
    }

  local combined_csv="$1"
  local topology_file="$2"

    NR == 1 { next }
    NF >= 3 {

      hop = $2 + 0

  hop_csv="$OUTPUT_DIR/${safe_host}.hop_ips.csv"

  echo "----------------------------------------------------------------"

content.text:
[[reply_to_current]] Updated the script to generate a text topology map.

It now creates:

```text
traceroute-results-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS/network_topology_map.txt
```

The map includes:

- paths by destination
- hop numbers and hop IPs
- `*` for missing/unresponsive hops
- observed hop-to-hop links
- notes for multiple IPs at the same hop, which can indicate ECMP/load balancing

Example shape:

```text
Network Topology Map
====================
Generated: 2026-05-20T10:43:00+00:00

Paths by destination
--------------------
fileserver.internal
  local
    -> [hop 1] 192.168.1.1
    -> [hop 2] 10.0.0.1
    -> [destination] fileserver.internal

Observed hop-to-hop links
-------------------------
local -> 192.168.1.1
192.168.1.1 -> 10.0.0.1
```

Run:

```bash
./traceroute_internal_hosts.sh
```

I also syntax-checked it and committed the script change:

```text

```
